_ruling: BK 2026-09-26 14:45 ruled the closed list of 12 (the Civic Principles card). BK 14:50 approved these four pairs ('yes'). Labels and definitions are copied word for word from the card (skills/unit0-print/build_civic_principles_card.py, PRINCIPLES). 'Consent of the Governed' and 'Sovereignty (self-government)' are retired as separate principles and folded into Popular Sovereignty.
scope_note: Four of the twelve, the ones 11.1 actually taught. Later units add pairs, always in the card's words.
intro: Match each principle to its definition.

right.label: No one is above the law, not even the people who make it.
Government can only do what the Constitution allows.
Government's power comes from the people, and it rules only with their agreement.
The people elect officials to make decisions for them.

rationale.a: Magna Carta: even the king had to follow the law.
rationale.b: Magna Carta capped the king's power. He could not raise taxes on his own.
rationale.c: In 11.1 you met this as consent of the governed. Same idea: power comes from the people.
rationale.d: Colonial assemblies: colonists elected their own lawmakers.
